rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the weighted average risk rating of loans was 2.3 and 2.3, respectively.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — compute the underlying composition shift behind the unchanged WA risk rating. Bucket-level counts and amortized cost by 1-5 rating, plus carry-forward into Q1 2025 10-Q for direction-of-travel.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text + claim_evolution (10-K Note 3 risk-rating table vs Q1 2025 10-Q Note 3)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Headline 2.3 is unchanged, but composition deteriorated: Risk-5 (Impaired/Loss Likely) went from 0 loans/$0 (YE23) -> 3 loans/$133.2M par (YE24), and 4-rated went from 6 loans/$271.9M to 1 loan/$56.6M. Total criticized (4+5) was 6 loans/$272M (5.4% of portfolio) at YE23 vs 4 loans/$192M (3.8%) at YE24 — superficially better, but only because 3 loans MIGRATED to rating-5 'Impaired/Loss Likely' rather than getting recovered. Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-04-28): 4-rated jumped to 5 loans/$167.6M (3.5%), 5-rated dropped to 1 loan/$22.1M (0.5%) — but the missing $111M of 5-rated loans went into REO via foreclosure, not into recovery. WA risk-rating reported as 2.2 (lower!) at Q1-25 only because $133M of bad assets transferred OFF the loan ledger to REO and CECL specific reserves were written off at foreclosure ($31.2M -> $1.1M of specific allowance).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Classic Mode B: the unchanged WA risk-rating headline obscures meaningful credit migration. The 'improvement' visible in Q1 2025 is mechanical — distressed assets exiting the loan book by becoming REO. Management discloses the components honestly (numbers are in the tables), but the headline framing is misleading and the 'flat 2.3' invites complacency.

rfm_tuples.R: The tax characteristics of $1.42 distributions per share of common stock declared during 2024 was $1.42 ordinary income... Basic earnings per share $0.82 (2024) vs $1.42 (2023)... Distributable earnings per share, fully converted: $0.92 (2024) vs $1.92 (2023).
rfm_tuples.f: Compute payout ratios on GAAP EPS and on non-GAAP Distributable Earnings (the management-preferred measure). Verify against Note 17 (Income Taxes) and Distributable Earnings reconciliation in Item 7.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text + Item 7 Distributable Earnings reconciliation + Note 17
rfm_tuples.M_value: 2024 dividend $1.42 / GAAP EPS $0.82 = 173% payout. 2024 dividend $1.42 / Distributable Earnings per share fully converted $0.92 = 154% payout. Distributable Earnings to Common fell 52% YoY ($169.5M -> $81.1M; per-share $1.92 -> $0.92). Even on the non-GAAP measure management itself defines as 'historically... an indicator of common dividends per share,' the dividend is unsustainable at current run-rate without external capital or asset sales. The MD&A footnote acknowledges '$11.9 million of GAAP loss adjustments that would run through distributable earnings if and when cash losses are realized' — a deferred drag on future DE.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Dividend exceeds both GAAP and non-GAAP earnings by 50-75%. This is a textbook distress signal for a mortgage REIT. Book value/share declined $0.62 (15.71 -> 15.09) consistent with overdistribution. The flat $1.42 dividend in a deteriorating earnings environment is a yield-anchor that creates capital pressure.

rfm_tuples.R: Non-performing loan amortized cost at beginning of year: $78.2M; Addition of non-performing loan amortized cost: $561.1M; Less: Removal of non-performing loan amortized cost: $506.1M; Non-performing loan amortized cost at end of period: $133.2M.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — the static endpoint of $133M conceals $561M of gross NPL inflow during 2024 (7.2x the opening balance). Compute the gross-flow ratio and verify against the 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Gross NPL inflow in 2024 = $561M = 11.3% of opening loan book ($4.94B). Gross NPL outflow = $506M (which includes $338M moved to REO and ~$168M repaid/restructured/sold). Q1 2025 10-Q rolls forward: opens at $133.2M, adds $91.4M (another 7%/quarter pace), removes $130.6M, ends at $94.0M. The 'three loans' headline at each reporting date masks rapid churn through the watchlist. Loans transferred to REO in Q1 2025 alone = $134.8M (per cash flow supplemental).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — a stable end-of-period NPL count (3 loans both YE23 and YE24, 3 loans at Q1-25) hides massive turnover. Management consistently frames distress as a handful of named office/multifamily loans, but the gross-flow rate (~11% of book/yr migrating through NPL status) is materially higher than the static stock would suggest.

rfm_tuples.R: The Company's real estate owned, held for sale assets include the remaining four retail properties in the Walgreens Portfolio... During the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company obtained 11 multifamily properties, in various locations throughout the United States, through foreclosure or deed-in-lieu of foreclosure and subsequently sold three of the properties.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify REO portfolio trajectory and the seller-financing tactic on REO dispositions (Mode B: how are these assets actually leaving the books?).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Note 5 + cash flow supplemental + subsequent events) + claim_evolution into Q1 2025 10-Q
rfm_tuples.M_value: REO held-for-sale: $103.7M (YE23, just Walgreens retail) -> $225.5M (YE24, +$211M of 11 multifamily REOs) -> $248.1M (Q1-25, added Denver CO office + 3 more multifamily, $360M including held-for-investment). Subsequent events: 'On February 12, 2025 for a purchase price of $63.8 million and was financed with a loan originated by the Company.' Q1 2025 10-Q cash-flow supplemental: 'Seller-based financing on sales of real estate owned, held for sale: $88,500' (thousand). So $88.5M of Q1 REO dispositions were financed BY FBRT itself — meaning the 'exit' is a balance-sheet recycle from REO into a new loan secured by the same building.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Critical Mode B finding. FBRT is clearing distressed CRE by lending the buyers their purchase price. The 10-K subsequent-events disclosure of the seller-financing is buried; the Q1 10-Q line item ($88.5M / one quarter) makes the scale concrete. This converts a credit-loss event into a fresh-vintage loan at presumably distressed valuations, deferring economic loss recognition into future periods. The maneuver is disclosed but not highlighted.

rfm_tuples.R: Total $535 million current sources of near-term liquidity as of December 31, 2024 (vs $1,524 million as of December 31, 2023): Unrestricted cash $184M (vs $338M); CLO reinvestment available $12M (vs $55M); Financings available & in progress $339M (vs $1,131M).
rfm_tuples.f: Verify liquidity trajectory and the timing of CLO reinvestment-period roll-offs, which determine whether the financing capacity is real.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Item 7 liquidity section) + CLO reinvestment-end dates table
rfm_tuples.M_value: Liquidity declined 65% YoY ($1.524B -> $535M). Five of six CLOs had already exited their reinvestment periods by YE24 (2021-FL6/FL7, 2022-FL8/FL9 all 'Ended'); 2023-FL10 ends 04/08/25 (3 weeks AFTER the 10-K filing and 5 weeks BEFORE cutoff). Only the new 2024-FL11 ($886M, raised 2024) is in reinvestment through 10/08/27. Without active reinvestment, CLOs cannot recycle paydowns into new loans — paydowns must amortize the CLO debt instead of being redeployed. The $12M of remaining reinvestment capacity is trivial vs. the $4.4B of CLO debt outstanding.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The liquidity narrative ('we closely monitor our liquidity position and believe that we have sufficient current liquidity... for the next 12 months and beyond') is technically true, but the COMPOSITION matters. The 65% decline + the structural exhaustion of CLO reinvestment capacity means new origination capacity is largely gone except via the brand-new 2024-FL11. With $338M of CLO financings in-progress unutilized at YE23 vs only $339M at YE24, capacity actually fell while balance-sheet pressure rose.

rfm_tuples.R: Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP... We have served as the Company's auditor since 2023. [And] /s/ Ernst & Young LLP... We served as the Company's auditor from 2017-2022. Item 9. Changes in and Disagreements With Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure: None.
rfm_tuples.f: auditor_change_tracker — verify the 2022->2023 EY->PwC handoff was clean and not associated with going-concern or material-weakness pressure.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Auditor change occurred between 2022 and 2023 (EY 2017-2022; PwC 2023+). Item 9 reports no disagreements. The 2024 10-K critical audit matter is the allowance for credit losses on commercial mortgage loans ($78.1M, including $31.2M of specific allowance for two office and one multifamily loan) — substantively the same risk area that subsequently exploded via the FY24 specific provisions and Q1 2025 foreclosures. No 'reportable events' or 8-K Item 4.01 disagreement filings surfaced for FBRT in the 2022-2023 transition window via routine review.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor change is real but no smoking gun on disagreements. Default-class change (EY -> PwC, both Big 4) is neutral. Worth flagging for context only — the CAM (ACL on commercial mortgage loans) is right in the danger zone for this issuer.

rfm_tuples.R: Insider trading pattern: 21 Form 4 filings in the 16 months before cutoff. CEO Byrne, President Comparato, CFO Baglien each filed January RSU-vest tax-withholding (Code F) sales; multiple director Code-A grants. No discretionary open-market sales (Code S).
rfm_tuples.f: insider_vs_calendar + form4 raw — check whether insiders are dumping ahead of capital events, repricing transactions, or quietly leaving.
rfm_tuples.M_source: form4 (raw EDGAR ownership.xml parse for 21 Form 4s, 2024-01-01 to 2025-05-15)
rfm_tuples.M_value: ZERO Code-S (discretionary open-market sales) by any officer or director in the 16-month pre-cutoff window. The only dispositions are Code-F tax-withholding on RSU vesting at predetermined dates (Jan 27, 2024 at $13.35 and Jan 27, 2025 at $12.44 — note the share price decline). All other transactions are Code-A equity grants. No 10b5-1 plan adoptions detected.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B insider check is clean. If officers genuinely believed the credit book was deteriorating beyond disclosure, you would expect either accelerated discretionary sales or 10b5-1 plan adoptions. Neither is present — the management team is increasing exposure via RSU grants. This is a partially offsetting positive signal that tempers the credit-deterioration concerns elsewhere.

rfm_tuples.R: Walgreens Portfolio... During the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company recorded a loss of $10.7 million related to the portfolio, consisting of a $9.7 million write-down of assets and a $1.0 million loss on the sale of 19 properties.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — the Walgreens REO is a structurally distressed single-tenant retail portfolio acquired in 2022 from a related-party JV. Verify cumulative loss trajectory and the related-party structure.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Walgreens JV partner is 'an affiliate of the Company' (Note 11 - Related Party Transactions). REO HFS retail went from 24 properties (YE22) -> 5 (YE24) -> 4 in 10-K language -> 3 (Q1 2025 10-Q). Cumulative losses: $4.0M impairment (2023) + $10.7M (2024) + $0.3M (Q1 2025) = $15.0M+ of disclosed losses on a single-tenant net-lease retail portfolio that should have been a low-volatility asset class. Original principal not directly disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Walgreens JV is a related-party transaction where FBRT and an affiliate share a deteriorating single-tenant retail portfolio. Cumulative losses are real and disclosed but the structure (assuming the loans then taking the REO via the JV) embeds related-party conflicts that are routine for externally-managed REITs but elevate forensic risk.

rfm_tuples.R: For the year ended December 31, 2024, the increase in specific reserve of $36.0 million was primarily related to two non-performing loans collateralized by office properties located in Colorado and Georgia... [Colorado] specific allowance for credit losses of $26.7 million on this loan for the year ended December 31, 2024... [Georgia] specific allowance for credit losses of $1.3 million.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive whether the $26.7M Colorado-office specific reserve is consistent with the $43.7M residual amortized cost (i.e., a 61% impairment). Verify against Q1 2025 disposition.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Colorado office: originated March 2021 with $48.5M commitment, amortized cost $43.7M, specific allowance $26.7M (61% reserve). Q1 2025 10-Q: 'The Company recorded a specific allowance for credit losses of [$XX] million on this loan for the year ended December 31, 2024... in [Q1 2025] the Company... [acquired] in the consolidated balance sheets. See Note 5 - Real Estate Owned for additional details. The Company charged off the specific allowance for credit losses at the time of the deed-in-lieu of foreclosure.' Colorado office now sits in REO HFS at $17.3M assets net — implying an effective realized loss in the range of $26M+ on a single $48.5M loan, or 54% LGD. Georgia office still at $22.1M amortized cost in cost-recovery status as of Q1 2025.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 61% reserve on the Colorado office and its subsequent migration to REO at less than half of par confirms a severe LGD case. This is acknowledged but the dollar realization is only $17.3M on the REO — meaning the eventual outcome is materially worse than even the 61% reserve implied. Office CRE realized severity is consistent with current cycle but the 10-K does not name the borrower or the city — verifiability requires post-cutoff data, so partially unverifiable at cutoff.

rfm_tuples.R: On January 16, 2025, the Articles Supplementary relating to the Series H Preferred Stock was amended such that the mandatory conversion date was extended by one year, to January 21, 2026.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — preferred-stock conversion extensions are often signals of capital-stack stress. Verify whether the extension was structured as a concession to the holder (the related-party Advisor affiliate per Note 11) and what the conversion ratio implies for dilution.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Series H Preferred: 5,370,498 shares of common per the fully-converted BVPS table; conversion ratio 299.2 common per Series H. The 1-year mandatory conversion extension (to Jan 21, 2026) was disclosed January 16, 2025. Series H is owned by Eldridge / NS9 (former Capstead Mortgage holder) — a related party. With FBRT common trading ~ $12.44 at the January 27, 2025 RSU-vest reference price and $15.09 BVPS, the holder is converting at a deep discount to book. The 1-year extension keeps the preferred (cumulative 4% min on $5,000 liq pref) outstanding — accruing $0.2M of monthly preferred dividend obligation that otherwise would have been replaced by common dilution.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — the extension is technical and disclosed, but its economic effect is to keep a senior, accretive instrument on the cap stack for another year at the holder's option, while the common is trading below book. This is mildly punitive to common holders and indicates the issuer (or holder) does not want to crystallize a $5M+ common dilution at current prices. Indirect signal that management sees current valuation as transient or that the related-party holder prefers the preferred yield to the common-equity exchange.

supplemental_signals.book_value_decline: Book value/share fell -3.9% YoY ($15.71 -> $15.09) at YE24, consistent with $0.60+/share of overdistribution vs. GAAP EPS.
supplemental_signals.criticized_loans_migration: Risk-5 (Impaired/Loss Likely) went from 0 to 3 loans/$133M par in 2024, then mechanically declined in Q1 25 only because the loans migrated to REO via foreclosure.
supplemental_signals.REO_growth: Total REO (HFI + HFS) grew $228.7M (2023) -> $338.6M (2024) -> $360.6M (Q1 2025) = ~7.5% of the loan book in distressed-asset overhang.
supplemental_signals.seller_financing_REO: $88.5M of Q1 2025 REO sales were financed by FBRT (creates fresh-vintage loans secured by recently-distressed assets).
supplemental_signals.CLO_reinvestment_exhaustion: 5 of 6 CLOs out of reinvestment period at YE24; only the new 2024-FL11 has active reinvestment until Oct 2027.
supplemental_signals.auditor_change: EY (2017-2022) -> PwC (2023+); no disclosed disagreements; CAM is the ACL on commercial mortgage loans.
supplemental_signals.insider_signal: No Code-S discretionary insider sales in 16 months pre-cutoff. Code-F (tax withholding on RSU vest) only, at declining reference prices ($13.35 in Jan 2024 -> $12.44 in Jan 2025).
supplemental_signals.related_party_count: Externally managed by Benefit Street Partners (Franklin Templeton sub). Walgreens REO JV with affiliate. Series H Preferred extension benefits related-party holder.

summary: FBRT is a Franklin Templeton-managed CRE mortgage REIT whose 10-K maintains an 'unchanged weighted-average risk rating of 2.3' headline that masks meaningful underlying credit deterioration: risk-5 loans jumped from 0 to 3 loans / $133M par in 2024, gross NPL inflow was $561M (~11% of book), and the Q1 2025 10-Q shows the credit problem migrating onto the balance sheet as REO ($226M -> $248M HFS in one quarter, plus $113M HFI). Critically, the $1.42 common dividend exceeded both GAAP EPS ($0.82, 173% payout) and management's own Distributable Earnings/share ($0.92 fully-converted, 154% payout), and book value/share declined $0.62 — a textbook sign of overdistribution. The strongest Mode B catch is the seller-financing tactic: $88.5M of Q1 2025 REO dispositions were financed by FBRT itself, converting credit losses into fresh-vintage loans rather than crystallizing them. Liquidity collapsed 65% YoY ($1.5B -> $535M) and 5 of 6 CLOs have exhausted reinvestment capacity. Partial offset: insiders show no discretionary selling. Verdict tilts SHORT-tier on dividend-coverage failure + REO-recycling + criticized-loan migration; size matters because management is honest in the footnotes even when the framing is misleading.
